commentary: Today, DCE iron ore futures trended weaker overall. The most-traded contract I2609 ulƟmately closed at 766.5 yuan/mt, down 1.35% from the previous trading session. Spot prices fell 5-8 yuan/mt from the previous trading day. Traders were only moderately acƟve in oﬀering quotes, while steel mills were cauƟous in procurement with fewer inquiries; spot market transacƟons remained mediocre so far. According to SMM survey data, daily average hot metal producƟon increased by 8,400 mt WoW this week, reaching 2.439 million mt. Blast furnace capacity uƟlizaƟon rate rose to 90.02%. The number of blast furnaces under maintenance decreased signiﬁcantly overall, providing strong support for rigid demand for iron ore in April. Despite the fundamentally favorable condiƟons, the overall market trend was sƟll inﬂuenced by news. Reports of breakthrough progress in negoƟaƟons triggered market concerns over potenƟal future supply, leading to downward pressure on prices. Meanwhile, persistently sluggish transacƟons in the spot market also weighed on the iron ore market. Overall, iron ore prices are expected to conƟnue a volaƟle and bearish trend going forward.
